textbookText: 2.3.3 Polygon Law of Vector Addition: Activity 1.1 i) Take a small piece of stone and displace it first by a displacement OA, then by AB, BC, CD, and finally to E, where E is the final point. ii) Join the initial point O with the final point E and determine the net displacement travelled by the stone you took. Clearly, the net displacement is OE, which is opposite to all the displacements and represents the resultant of all the displacements. This technique is known as the polygon law of vector addition. Statement: If the forces (vectors) acting on a particle are represented by the sides of a polygon in magnitude and order, then the closing side of the polygon taken in the opposite order represents the resultant of the vectors.

Then using the triangle law of vector addition on a⃗⃗ and−b⃗⃗, we get the resultant R⃗⃗ as R⃗⃗ =a⃗⃗ −b⃗⃗. The triangle law in the fig. indicates the difference between a⃗⃗ +b⃗⃗ and a⃗⃗ -b⃗⃗ .

C. Resolution of a Vector: Resolution is the reverse process of the addition of vectors. In resolution, a vector is split into two or more vectors as components of the original vector. The component of a vector is the effective part of the vector in the direction taken. Generally, it is expressed as the magnitude of the vector times, the cosine of the angle between the vector and the component vector.

a. Scalar and vector Products

Activity 1.3 i) Take any two natural numbers and multiply them; the result is called a scalar, and the multiplication is referred to as the scalar product of the two vectors. ii) Take a screw and rotate it clockwise, then note the direction of the advancement. iii) Repeat the same process in the anticlockwise direction, and once again note the direction of advancement.

In the first case of screw rotation, it advances downwards, while in the latter case it advances upwards, indicating a specific direction in each instance. This product is known as the vector product or the cross product of the two vectors.
Physics, Grade 11 | 30
The physical significance of both these is actually a beautiful concept.

For example, in your airplane case, a dot product would give the combined effect of the coordinates in different dimensions on each other. A cross product would actually help you discover and identify a new path, which would be normal to both the vectors you mentioned.

The cross product could help you identify the path, which would result in the most damage if a bird hits the aeroplane through it. The dot product could give you the interference of sound waves produced by the revving of an engine on the journey.
